title: Erasure law for transition tables
statement: For every natural number $n$ and bit string $x$, decoding a transition table for $n+1$ states, three possible input-symbol values on each of three symbol-indexed dimensions, and actions of a two-work-tape machine has the same success or failure and leaves the same suffix as skipping the encoding of that table. In other words, discarding the decoded table from the reader gives exactly the result of the corresponding table skipper.
